source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #339 (branch fix/192-shared-lowering at head ea36972ab1c5b87625228f1d48248593e8bade4e — the #192 change (the three baseline JIT backends merged into one shared lowering over a per-target BaselineMasm trait, plus the Codex P1 fix mapping the inverted condition through cond_code in AArch64 cset_w; commits 8b94d2e, 8b34d6c, 54553ad, 97bba04 and ea36972) merged with current main 726fdd964b5b6c5dd264397d8616154cb7a9b242 (PRs #329 and #337); ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45545862796, 45545874933 and 45546994821 against the branch and pull-request run 45545862499, which built the same tree; the four samples agree on every core-jit value, and the recorded values are the medians across the samples
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #339 (#192, the three baseline JIT backends (x86_64, aarch64, riscv64) merged into one shared lowering generic over a per-target BaselineMasm trait; the branch also carries the Codex P1 fix for that lowering: AArch64 cset_w emitted the inverted condition from the shared semantic Cond discriminant instead of the target encoding, fixed by mapping through cond_code). Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45541261935, 45541270512 and 45541278948 on main at 726fdd964b5b6c5dd264397d8616154cb7a9b242; all three runs pass the gate). The main control reproduces the checked-in baseline exactly on all 32 gated series, so no part of the gate failure is main-side staleness. This PR's own delta against the main control is confined to core-jit, the only embedder configuration that links the JIT backends: in release, stripped file +576 B and stripped .text +384 B; in release-size, stripped file -64 B and stripped .text +112 B. Every other configuration is byte-identical to main in both profiles in the three workflow_dispatch samples. The pull-request run (45545862499), which built the same tree, measured the three component configurations (component, wasi, wasi-threads) 848 to 2,344 B lower than every other sample; no part of this PR touches the component layer, and the three dispatch samples agree with the main control byte-for-byte on those series, so the recorded values for them are the medians across the four branch samples, which equal the main control. Run-to-run spread across the four branch samples was 0 B for the core-jit series and for the 16 series of the baseline, core, core-nosimd and core-aot configurations, and across the three main samples it was 0 B for every gated series. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth remains the release component stripped file series at +9.85% (2,433,656 B to 2,673,368 B), which this PR does not change; the release core-nosimd stripped file series stays at +9.83% (1,275,448 B to 1,400,840 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
